title: [FMLA 05] NormalQ — Normal Probability Q(x)
summary: Standard normal probability from 0 to x (Casio Q; Hastings approximation). Prompt is x; range 0 ≤ x < 10⁵⁰.

body.text: Calculator scroll name: NormalQ. The prompt is x. Q(x) is the area under the standard normal curve from 0 to x — that is P(0 ≤ Z ≤ x), not the upper tail from x to +∞.
Q(x) is the slab between the mean (0) and x. For x = 1 that slab is about 0.3413. NormalP is the whole left side including this slab: P(1) = 0.5 + Q(1) ≈ 0.8413.

body.caption: Same bell as NormalP. Q(x) is the shaded area from 0 to x. Here x = 1, so Q(1) ≈ 0.3413 = P(0 ≤ Z ≤ 1).

body.title: How to run
items: Press FMLA, then 0, then 5 (or scroll to the name and EXE)

body.label: Limits
body.text: Hastings-style approximation. Official range is 0 ≤ x < 1×10⁵⁰. The printed integral uses |x|; still enter a non-negative x. For a left-of-mean interval, use symmetry: P(−a ≤ Z ≤ 0) = Q(a).
